reading.body:
Rand Paul's recorded AI-related activity is one bill, S. 2296, and one $2,000 PAC contribution from Meta Platforms.

The thirteen events are almost entirely procedural votes on a single piece of legislation. Ten of them fall on one day, 2025-10-09, and consist of votes on amendments to S. 2296 plus passage of the bill. The earlier three, from September 2025, are votes on whether to proceed and on a motion to table an amendment. Paul voted Nay on final passage and Nay on the procedural steps, and Yea on several amendments. The record shows a consistent pattern of opposition to the bill itself rather than a set of separate AI positions.

The only money in the record is a $2,000 contribution from Meta Platforms' PAC in March 2025. That is a small sum by federal standards and the data does not say what, if anything, it purchased. It is also the only corporate AI money listed, so no comparison across companies or cycles is possible here.

Two news stories name the record, one on a Newsom executive order about an AI kill switch and one on King Charles warning about AI dangers. Neither is a vote or a filing, and the data does not establish that Paul acted on either. What the record does not contain is as important as what it does: no sponsored AI bills, no committee chairmanship on the subject, and no votes on data center power, grid interconnection, or compute permitting. On the question this site cares about most, whether the grid is the binding constraint on AI scaling, this record is silent.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Rand Paul: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 13 events, and 2 news stories that name them.
